title: Preserve GLM partial results and lifecycle bookkeeping
description: A GLM run returned a structured partial result after 27m07s with exit code 1, but the MCP wrapper marked it isError=true. The normal PostToolUse finish hook was not recorded, leaving agent-evals running and prompting the parent to stop despite AGENTS.md requiring native fallback.
acceptance_criteria: Structured partial worker output is returned as non-transport-error status=partial even with a nonzero process exit; focused tests cover wrapper formatting; the current stale run is recovered and labelable; AGENTS.md explicitly requires recovery plus native/local continuation after partial/error/timeout.
close_reason: Fixed MCP classification for structured partial results, added durable patching and 11 passing regression/integration tests, reconciled and labeled the affected run, strengthened project recovery guidance, and passed review-mcp.

title: Prevent GLM worker timeout result loss
description: The independent GLM worker has twice reached the configured 10-minute ceiling. Completed edits can remain in the shared worktree while the parent receives no usable result, and assistant output is lost because sub-agents-mcp only structures terminal result events.
design: Patch the pinned local sub-agents-mcp 0.12.1 runtime through an idempotent postinstall script, test StreamProcessor/timeout integration behavior with Node tests, and configure a 30-minute worker ceiling with a larger outer MCP tool timeout.
acceptance_criteria: Raise internal GLM execution timeout and outer MCP timeout coherently; return accumulated Claude-compatible assistant text as a structured partial result on internal timeout; make the runtime patch survive npm reinstall; add and pass focused regression tests; obtain review-mcp review.
close_reason: Implemented durable timeout recovery, raised coordinated ceilings, passed 8 regression/integration tests, and completed review-mcp review.

title: Provenance-kernel architectural pass: name and spec the domain-neutral core
description: Why: on 2026-10-03 the project adopted the provenance-kernel direction (docs/plans/provenance-kernel.md) — the north star broadened from a cross-platform media catalog to a source-aware gathering and provenance system with media as the first data family. The kernel already exists latently in the schema (platforms, raw_observations/raw_payloads, five run families, CAS assets, evidence/decision ledgers) but has no name, spec, or boundary. What needs to be done: (1) verify the kernel-to-schema mapping table in the plan against the actual migrations, per table; (2) add an OpenSpec kernel capability spec covering source and source-object identity, observation retention and revisions, the run/checkpoint contract, the evidence and review ledger, blobs, and typed relationships with epistemic status (observed/verified/derived/inferred/reviewed); (3) re-home or name module and spec boundaries where cheap, absorbing the two ready persistence follow-ups (adoption_items read into StorageWrites; single-family vocabulary colocation); (4) reconcile the observations vs raw_observations naming in the kernel vocabulary; (5) decide where the kernel spec boundary lives (standalone capability spec vs media-catalog-core sections). Constraints: no table renames, no data migration, no adapter behavior changes, no speculative abstractions without a second consumer.
notes: Task 1.2 cross-check complete (2026-10-03): walked each of the 12 provenance-kernel requirements against kernel plan section 2 mapping rows — all correspond (R1 identity<->Source/Source-object, R2 source reports, R3 provenance events, R4 blobs, R5 comparisons<->Assertion row, R6 relationships, R7 evidence, R8 review, R9 bounded runs<->Run+disciplines, R10 immutability<->discipline 1, R11 projections, R12 forward-looking). No requirement/mapping disagreements found; strict openspec validation passes.
close_reason: Architectural pass complete 2026-10-03: mapping verified against migrations 0001-0011 with corrections folded into the kernel plan; standalone provenance-kernel capability spec (12 requirements, review-corrected) synced into main specs and archived as 2026-10-03-add-provenance-kernel-spec; boundary re-homing done via beads v4i+ee0 (both closed); observations/raw_observations naming reconciled; spec boundary decided as standalone capability. Enforcement follow-up filed as data-processing-ts5. Gates green: pytest, ruff check, ty check, openspec validate --specs (15 capabilities).

title: Add bounded Gelbooru metadata adapter
description: Create and implement the add-gelbooru-metadata-adapter OpenSpec. Support two explicit metadata transports: credentialed JSON DAPI and anonymous HTML for individually requested posts. Preserve raw provenance and neutral normalized facts, keep credentials external, make all network work bounded and auditable, and do not silently change transports. Initial scope excludes media acquisition, broad crawling, automatic identity/authorship, similarity, cross-database aliases, and unproven artist/library capabilities.
acceptance_criteria: OpenSpec proposal, design, delta specs, and tasks are complete and strictly valid. Implementation later provides fixture-backed explicit DAPI and HTML metadata paths with typed failures, privacy boundaries, no implicit media downloads, compatibility coverage, documentation, and review.
notes:
Progress: 37/37 tasks complete. Task 3.4 implemented and review-hardened.

3.4 implementation (33b58e6): fully scope-validated continuations — all 7 dimensions carried and validated before network; continuation version gelbooru-pid-v1 → v2; scope embedded in identity/request_target; 13 dimension tests; gallery-dl extractor was the interaction reference.

3. Missing rejection tests for in-value continuation/adapter version material — added.

All gates green: full suite, ruff, ty, OpenSpec validation. Commits: befdb5a, d06f587, 33b58e6, fea5588.

title: Close provenance-kernel storage-enforcement gaps
description: Why: the schema-accuracy review of the provenance-kernel spec (2026-10-03) found that several kernel invariants currently rest on writer convention rather than storage constraints, and the kernel spec intentionally binds ahead of enforcement (its Purpose states storage enforcement is tracked as follow-up). What needs to be done, as one bounded migration change when taken: (1) append-only enforcement for raw_observations and post_tag_observations (no-update/no-delete triggers, matching tag_observations from migration 0009); (2) terminal-immutability triggers for remote_requests and adoption_attempts (matching candidate_lookup_requests 0007 and media_acquisition_attempts 0006); (3) immutable-inputs trigger for remote_runs covering platform/instance/operation/target/versions/budgets/started_at (matching candidate_lookup_runs 0007 and media_acquisition_runs 0006; today only origin columns are protected); (4) protect the review/evidence ledger against cascade destruction (candidate deletion currently cascades to decisions and evidence links, so the storage layer permits destroying review history the spec requires to survive); (5) consider an observations append-only trigger. Constraints: new migration(s) only, no data changes, no table renames; each trigger needs focused tests attempting the mutation. The epistemic-status columns are NOT part of this bead — they land with the relationship model (kernel plan Phase D).

Adoption read logic is split across two places. Move the query into StorageWrites and keep an identical-signature delegation on the facade, mirroring the other extractions. Raised as P3 by the change's bounded review; deferred to keep the refactor change behavior-only.
close_reason: Absorbed into the add-provenance-kernel-spec OpenSpec change (architectural pass, data-processing-u1d): adoption_items read moved into StorageWrites with the facade delegating (v4i); single-family vocabulary+validator pairs colocated with acquisition/lookup/library/storage family modules, facade surface unchanged, cross-family origin-kind pair kept in common (ee0). Full gates green: pytest, ruff check, ty check.

title: Colocate single-family vocabularies and validators with their record family modules
description: Review of the record split (task 4.4, modularize-catalog-persistence) found records/common.py absorbs every domain's vocabulary and validators, including ones consumed by exactly one family (all 12 validate_acquisition_* only by acquisition.py, all 8 validate_library_* only by library.py, all 8 validate_lookup_* only by lookup.py, adoption/storage likewise). This re-grows the god-module the refactor set out to kill and makes each new state a 5-6 edit-site change. Design rule says records.common should hold only high-fan-in primitives. Move each single-family vocabulary+validator pair into its family module (families import validators only, never vocabularies, so pairs are cohesive), keep true cross-family primitives (validate_platform, validate_hash, normalize_timestamp, _validate_*, shared patterns) in common. The __init__ re-export surface and pinned digests can stay byte-identical, making this free now and expensive later. Should run as its own slice with focused gates and review.
close_reason: Absorbed into the add-provenance-kernel-spec OpenSpec change (architectural pass, data-processing-u1d): adoption_items read moved into StorageWrites with the facade delegating (v4i); single-family vocabulary+validator pairs colocated with acquisition/lookup/library/storage family modules, facade surface unchanged, cross-family origin-kind pair kept in common (ee0). Full gates green: pytest, ruff check, ty check.
